Performers
Arthur Whittemore (piano), Jack Lowe (piano), RCA Victor Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), Dimitri Mitropoulos (conductor) Documented

The original labels and RCA’s contemporary advertisement name all four performing credits. The sources consulted do not allocate the first and second piano parts to the individual pianists.

[3] [4] [5]
Work version
Original orchestral scoring; complete second movement Documented

The transfer joins the two 78-rpm sides containing the Larghetto. The source identifies the original concerto, not a piano reduction. The exact edition used by the performers is unknown. The section landmarks are provisional passage timings, established from the score and the transfer; they have not been reviewed by ear.

[1] [3] [4] [6]
Recorded
1947 Documented

The transfer description gives 15 December 1947. The year is retained here; the exact day has not been checked against a session ledger. The item-level date 1947 is the recording year, not the commercial publication year.

[1]
Place
NBC Studio 3-A, New York City, United States Documented

Venue as identified by the transfer description.

[1]
Label
RCA Victor Red Seal Documented

Original shellac-record imprint.

[3] [4]
Catalogue
DM-1235; record 12-0368 Documented

The automatic-sequence album contains three 12-inch records. RCA’s September 1948 magazine advertises both M-1235 and DM-1235. The Larghetto occupies record 12-0368 in the transferred DM set.

[3] [4] [5]
Matrix, take, sides
Sides 3–⁠4: 12-0368-A and 12-0368-B; matrices D7-RC-8226 and D7-RC-8227 Documented

Side and record numbers were read on the labels, which also print the corresponding manual-sequence numbers 12-0364-A/B. Matrix numbers are transcribed from the transfer description; no take suffix or stamper has been established.

[1] [3] [4]
Transfer
Internet Archive, Shellackophile Recordings collection Documented

Host and collection are identified. The original record producer is RCA; no separate personal transfer-engineer credit has been established.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item was uploaded on 3 April 2022. Its digitisation date is not stated.

[1]
Processing
Uploaded FLAC transfer; Internet Archive VBR MP3 derivative Documented

The complete-movement MP3 derives from the uploaded FLAC. Playback equipment, side-join method, equalisation, pitch correction and noise reduction are not documented.

[2]
Composition rights
Separate composition copyright remains in force in life-plus-70 territories; IMSLP identifies public-domain status in Canada. Documented

Poulenc died in 1963. IMSLP explicitly warns that this work remains protected in the EU and probably in the US. The accepted historical-phonogram rule below does not clear the underlying composition; no separate permission or worldwide composition licence has been established.

[7] [8]
Recording rights
Territorial EU public-domain basis: commercial publication in 1948, before 1963. Documented

RCA’s September 1948 magazine advertises M/DM-1235 with performers, format and prices. Under the project’s pre-1963 phonogram rule, the former 50-year term expired before the 2013 extension. The recording is not offered under a Creative Commons licence; US recording status is not established.

[5] [1] [9]

Francis Poulenc, Concerto for Two Pianos, FP 61: II. Larghetto; Arthur Whittemore and Jack Lowe, RCA Victor Symphony Orchestra, Dimitri Mitropoulos. Recorded 1947; RCA Victor Red Seal DM-1235, published 1948. Shellackophile collection / Internet Archive transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; the underlying composition remains separately protected.

  1. Internet Archive — Poulenc Double Concerto, Whittemore and Lowe, 1947 — Description distinguishes the 15 December 1947 session in NBC Studio 3-A from the 1948 issue; gives carrier and matrix details. Collection and 2022 upload date are separate metadata.. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  2. Internet Archive — Larghetto derivative and source FLAC — DM1235 Poulenc Double Concerto (ii).mp3, 404.77 seconds; derivative of the complete-movement FLAC, 404.72 seconds.. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  3. RCA Victor DM-1235 — original side 3 label — 12-0368-A, side 3; Larghetto, part 1; Whittemore, Lowe, RCA Victor Symphony Orchestra and Dimitri Mitropoulos.. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  4. RCA Victor DM-1235 — original side 4 label — 12-0368-B, side 4; Larghetto, concluded; same performers as side 3.. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  5. RCA Victor Record Review, September 1948 — Music of Poulenc — PDF p. 6 advertises the recorded première as M/DM-1235, three 12-inch RCA Victor records, and names the pianists, orchestra and conductor. Cover and masthead establish September 1948.. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  6. Poulenc — Concerto for Two Pianos, full score — Rouart, Lerolle & Cie., plate R.L. 11887, Larghetto pp. 37–⁠63. Opening, Plus allant at rehearsal 34, Tempo I on p. 59 and the closing page inspected visually. Score used for research, not republished.. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  7. IMSLP — Concerto for Two Pianos, FP 61 — 1932 composition, 1933 publication, movement titles and instrumentation; explicit Canada versus EU/US composition-rights warning.. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  8. Steven Ledbetter — Boston Symphony note on Poulenc's Two-⁠Piano Concerto — Poulenc's dates, the Polignac commission, Venice première and the composer's explanation of the Mozartian Larghetto opening.. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  9. Directive 2011/77/EU — phonogram term and transition — Recitals 1–⁠3 and Article 1(2)–(3): former 50-year phonogram term and extension for recordings still protected on 1 November 2013.. Accessed 2026-10-19.
